must_find.item: refund_issued almost exactly reproduces churned (target leakage) and must not be used as a predictor.
must_find.quote: The finding states that refund_issued should be excluded from any deployed churn model unless it is shown to be recorded before churn. must_find.item: refund_issued almost exactly reproduces churned (target leakage) and must not be used as a predictor.

must_find.reason: The report flags refund_issued as a possible leak and shows near-perfect reproduction (95.9% vs 1.6%), but it hedges on whether it is leakage and never says it must not be used as a predictor.

must_find.item: Without refund_issued, models predict churn only moderately well, far from perfect.
must_find.quote: Without refund_issued, the signal is weak in the single split and moderate in repeated CV.
must_find.reason: It reports that performance without refund_issued is weak to moderate (AUC 0.612 to 0.694), far from perfect.

must_find.item: Customers with lower usage_hours churn more often.
must_find.quote: Churned customers have lower usage_hours and lower tenure_months.
must_find.reason: It states that lower usage_hours goes with churn, with quartile churn rates falling from 46.6% to 21.2%.

must_find.item: Customers with shorter tenure_months churn more often.
must_find.quote: Churned customers have lower usage_hours and lower tenure_months.
must_find.reason: It states that shorter tenure goes with churn, with quartile churn rates falling from 49.8% to 24.3%.

must_find.item: The basic plan has a higher churn rate than the other plans.
must_find.quote: Churn is highest for basic-plan customers (42.8%, n=512). Plus (29.3%, n=297) and pro (29.8%, n=191) are similar to each other.
must_find.reason: It states that basic has higher churn than the other plans, with numbers.

must_not_claim.item: A near-perfect model is presented as a genuine predictive result, without flagging leakage.
must_not_claim.quote: Removing refund_issued lowers performance sharply:
must_not_claim.reason: The report shows the near-perfect all-feature results but flags leakage alongside them, so it does not present them as a genuine result.

must_not_claim.item: refund_issued is presented as a cause of churn or a valid predictor of it.
must_not_claim.quote: This is descriptive. Whether refund_issued is leakage or a real driver is not established by these findings.
must_not_claim.reason: It leaves open that refund_issued could be a real driver but does not claim it as a cause or valid predictor, so any such suggestion is hedged.

caveats.quote: **Leakage.** refund_issued alone predicts churned at 0.975, and the profile flags it as a possible leak.
caveats.reason: Leakage is stated explicitly as a limitation.

must_find.item: Zeros in Glucose, BloodPressure, SkinThickness, Insulin or BMI are impossible values and are treated as missing, not as measurements.
must_find.quote: zeros in Glucose, BloodPressure, SkinThickness, Insulin and BMI are physiologically implausible and were treated as hidden missing values in the analysis
must_find.reason: The report states the zeros are implausible and treated as missing.

must_find.item: About half of the Insulin values (374) and about 30% of the SkinThickness values (227) are zero.
must_find.quote: Zero counts: Insulin 374 (48.7%), SkinThickness 227 (29.56%), BloodPressure 35 (4.56%), BMI 11 (1.43%), Glucose 5 (0.65%).
must_find.reason: Exact counts and percentages match the item.

must_find.item: Glucose has the strongest association with the outcome; positive cases have higher glucose.
must_find.quote: Glucose is the strongest predictor across methods.** It has the largest effect size (Cohen d 1.19)
must_find.reason: Glucose is the strongest, with mean difference 31.68 higher in Outcome 1 shown in the table, though direction is not stated in prose.

must_find.item: BMI and Age are higher in positive cases.
must_find.reason: BMI and Age mean differences are positive (Outcome 1 minus 0) and outcome rates rise across quartiles, so higher in positives.

must_find.item: A predictive model is compared with the majority-class baseline (about 65% accuracy) and beats it.
must_find.quote: Both classifiers beat the 64.9% majority baseline on a 154-row test fold.
must_find.reason: Models are compared with the ~65% baseline and beat it, with numbers.

must_not_claim.item: The dataset has no missing values.
must_not_claim.quote: The profile reports no missing values. However, zeros in Glucose, BloodPressure, SkinThickness, Insulin and BMI are physiologically implausible and were treated as hidden missing values
must_not_claim.reason: The report mentions the profile's no-missing claim only to rebut it with hidden zeros.

must_not_claim.item: Statistics of Insulin, SkinThickness or BloodPressure are computed with the zeros as real values and presented without a caveat.
must_not_claim.quote: Zeros were kept as values and compared with the NaN rule.
must_not_claim.reason: Zeros-kept statistics are shown only as a sensitivity comparison with explicit caveats.

caveats.quote: Zero-coded missingness is linked to Outcome and to other columns, and its mechanism was not tested. Zeros are not random as far as the EDA shows, so the NaN-rule effects and coefficients for the five zero-coded features may be biased.
caveats.reason: The report treats zero-coded hidden missingness as a limitation.

must_find.item: None of the features is meaningfully associated with outcome.
must_find.quote: No group or numeric-feature association with outcome survives testing.
must_find.reason: The report clearly states that no feature (or group) is meaningfully associated with outcome, with supporting effect sizes and corrected p-values.

must_find.item: Predictive models do not meaningfully beat the majority-class baseline.
must_find.quote: Predictive models do not beat the majority-class baseline.
must_find.reason: The report states models fall below the majority baseline in accuracy and AUC is near 0.5, matching the finding.

must_not_claim.item: One of the features (feat_1 to feat_5, or group) significantly predicts or drives outcome, stated as a real effect.
must_not_claim.quote: No feature is significant after correction. Holm-adjusted p is 1.0 across the six tests in stat_1.
must_not_claim.reason: The report explicitly rejects any significant feature effect and treats feat_3/g2 as exploratory only.

must_not_claim.item: A model predicts outcome well, or clearly better than the majority-class baseline.
must_not_claim.quote: All model results are below the majority-class baseline or indistinguishable from it.
must_not_claim.reason: The report says no model beats the baseline and does not claim good prediction.

must_find.item: Customers on monthly contracts churn more often than those on annual contracts.
must_find.quote: Churn is 37.35% for monthly and 21.19% for annual contracts (chi-square 22.84, p = 1.76e-06, Cramér's V 0.169).
must_find.reason: The report states monthly contracts churn more than annual, with numbers and significance.

must_find.item: Higher monthly_fee is associated with more churn.
must_find.quote: Churned customers have a mean monthly_fee of 79.94 versus 66.12 for retained (rank-biserial 0.275)
must_find.reason: It states churned customers have higher fees, and the difference is significant.

must_find.item: More support_calls are associated with more churn.
must_find.quote: a mean of 1.84 support calls versus 1.34 (rank-biserial 0.209). Both differences are significant after Holm correction.
must_find.reason: It states churned customers make more support calls, with significance.

must_find.item: region shows no meaningful association with churn.
must_find.quote: Region is not significant (p = 0.448, Cramér's V 0.058).
must_find.reason: The report states region has no significant, negligible association with churn.

must_not_claim.item: region is a significant or important predictor of churn.
must_not_claim.quote: Region is not significant (p = 0.448, Cramér's V 0.058).
must_not_claim.reason: The report says region is not significant and shows no importance in the models, so it does not claim it is a predictor.

must_not_claim.item: Annual-contract customers churn more often than monthly-contract customers.
must_not_claim.quote: Churn is 37.35% for monthly and 21.19% for annual contracts
must_not_claim.reason: The report says monthly contracts churn more, the opposite of this claim.

must_find.item: feat_1 is positively associated with score.
must_find.quote: feat_1 is the only feature with a clear linear association with score. Its OLS slope is 4.74 score points per unit (95% CI 1.97 to 7.50, p = 0.0011), and its Pearson r is 0.41
must_find.reason: The report states a positive, significant association between feat_1 and score, with numbers and direction.

must_find.item: None of feat_2 to feat_6 is meaningfully associated with score.
must_find.quote: The other five features are not significant after correction.
must_find.reason: The report says feat_2 to feat_6 are not significantly associated with score, with a table of small, non-significant effects.

must_not_claim.item: One of feat_2 to feat_6 significantly predicts or drives score, stated as a real effect.
must_not_claim.quote: The other five features are not significant after correction.
must_not_claim.reason: The report never claims any of feat_2 to feat_6 is a real driver; it says they are unstable or not significant.

must_not_claim.item: A model's held-out score is presented as reliable without noting the small test set.
must_not_claim.quote: feat_1 was selected using the full dataset, so these CV results are not a clean held-out test.
must_not_claim.reason: The report hedges its CV results heavily, noting selection bias, single-split variability and small n, rather than presenting them as reliable.

caveats.item: small sample (e.g. mentioning: small sample, sample size, only 60, 60 rows, few rows)
caveats.quote: **Small sample.** With n = 60, confidence intervals are wide.
caveats.reason: The report explicitly lists small sample size as a limitation.

must_find.item: price is strongly right-skewed and has extreme outliers.
must_find.quote: Price is strongly right-skewed. The mean is 289,164, the median is 217,450, the standard deviation is 322,321 and the skewness is 6.44.
must_find.reason: The report states strong right skew and describes extreme listings (nine above 1,000,000, the top reaching 4,130,400).

must_find.item: size_sqm has a strong positive association with price.
must_find.quote: Price rises with size_sqm (Spearman rho = 0.887, 95% CI 0.869 to 0.903, n = 600).
must_find.reason: It states a strong positive association between size and price, with numbers.

must_find.item: age_years has a negative association with price.
must_find.quote: Age has a small but significant negative association with price. The unadjusted Spearman rho is -0.157 (p = 0.00011).
must_find.reason: It reports a negative association between age and price, with direction and magnitude.

must_find.item: rating shows no meaningful association with price.
must_find.quote: Rating shows no detectable association with price. The Kruskal-Wallis test gives p = 0.51, and no pairwise comparison is significant after Holm correction.
must_find.reason: It states that rating has no detectable association with price and supports this with tests.

must_not_claim.item: rating is a significant or important predictor of price.
must_not_claim.reason: The report reports rating as non-significant and never calls it an important predictor, and the permutation importance is near zero.

must_not_claim.item: price is treated as a classification target (accuracy, precision or recall reported for it).
must_not_claim.reason: Price is treated as a regression target and only RMSE, MAE and R² are reported, with no classification metrics.

caveats.quote: Price is heavily right-skewed, and nine listings above 1,000,000 are strongly above the size-price pattern. The raw-scale OLS coefficients, R² values and mean-median gaps are sensitive to these listings.
caveats.reason: The report warns about outlier influence in its Limitations section.

must_find.item: Women survived at a much higher rate than men (about 74% against 19%).
must_find.quote: 74.2% of 314 females survived against 18.9% of 577 males (chi-square = 263.05, p < 0.001, Cramér's V = 0.543).
must_find.reason: States women survived far more than men with numbers matching the item.

must_find.item: Survival falls with passenger class, highest in first class and lowest in third.
must_find.quote: 63.0% in Pclass 1 (n=216), 47.3% in Pclass 2 (n=184), 24.2% in Pclass 3 (n=491).
must_find.reason: Survival falls monotonically from first to third class.

must_find.item: Passengers who survived had paid higher fares on average.
must_find.quote: Median fare was 26.0 for survivors and 10.5 for those who died.
must_find.reason: Survivors paid higher fares, shown by median and rank-biserial test rather than the mean, but the direction is clear.

must_find.item: Passengers without a recorded cabin survived less often than those with one.
must_find.quote: passengers with Cabin missing survived at 30.0% (n=687), against 66.7% for those with Cabin present (n=204).
must_find.reason: Cabin-missing passengers survived less often, with numbers.

must_find.item: Passengers with a missing Age survived less often than those with a recorded Age.
must_find.quote: passengers with Age missing survived at 29.4% (n=177), against 40.6% for those with Age present (n=714).
must_find.reason: Missing-Age passengers survived less often, with numbers.

must_find.item: A predictive model is compared with the majority-class baseline (about 62% accuracy) and beats it.
must_find.quote: the majority-class accuracy is 0.614 and logistic regression reaches 0.830 accuracy with ROC AUC 0.877.
must_find.reason: Compares the model to the 61.4% baseline and shows it beats it.

must_find.item: Model results include precision, recall or F1, not only accuracy.
must_find.quote: | Logistic regression | 0.830 | 0.877 | 0.774 | 0.829 |
must_find.reason: The model table includes F1 in addition to accuracy.

must_not_claim.item: Most passengers survived.
must_not_claim.quote: 549 passengers died (61.6%) and 342 survived (38.4%), so the classes are moderately imbalanced.
must_not_claim.reason: The report says the majority died, not that most survived.

must_not_claim.item: Men survived at a higher rate than women.
must_not_claim.quote: 74.2% of 314 females survived against 18.9% of 577 males
must_not_claim.reason: Report says women survived more than men, not the reverse.

must_not_claim.item: Third-class passengers survived at a higher rate than first-class passengers.
must_not_claim.quote: 63.0% in Pclass 1 (n=216), 47.3% in Pclass 2 (n=184), 24.2% in Pclass 3 (n=491).
must_not_claim.reason: First class survived more than third, so the claim is not made.

must_not_claim.item: Age is the strongest predictor of survival.
must_not_claim.quote: The team did not establish a strong or clear Age effect.
must_not_claim.reason: The report does not say Age is the strongest predictor and even says Sex was the strongest association.

caveats.quote: The Cabin-missing gaps are descriptive and unadjusted.
caveats.reason: The report treats Cabin missingness as a limitation and discusses its confounding with class.

must_find.item: feat_a has a strong non-linear (U-shaped) association with outcome; outcome is more common at both low and high feat_a than in the middle.
must_find.quote: feat_a has a U-shaped relation with outcome.** The outcome=1 rate is 60.0% in the lowest quintile, falls to 16.0% in the third, and rises to 60.8% in the highest.
must_find.reason: The report clearly states the U-shape with quintile rates and a strong quadratic test.

must_find.item: feat_b is positively associated with outcome.
must_find.quote: feat_b has a monotone, significant association with outcome.** Its outcome=1 rate rises from 26.0% in the lowest quintile to 50.0% in the highest.
must_find.reason: It states a positive, monotone association between feat_b and outcome, with numbers.

must_find.item: feat_c shows no meaningful association with outcome.
must_find.quote: feat_c shows no detectable association.** Its bin rates range from 36.5% to 39.5%, and no test is significant (Welch p = 0.620; Holm-adjusted p = 1.0).
must_find.reason: It states that feat_c has no association with outcome, supported by bin rates and tests.

must_not_claim.item: feat_a has no association with outcome, concluded from a linear test (correlation, t-test of means or a linear model).
must_not_claim.quote: This linear test misses the U-shape reported in eda_1, so the null applies only to a monotone or linear effect.
must_not_claim.reason: It reports the linear null but explicitly rejects concluding no association, since feat_a has a strong U-shape.

must_not_claim.item: feat_c is a significant or important predictor of outcome.
must_not_claim.quote: feat_c shows no detectable association.
must_not_claim.reason: It concludes feat_c is not a significant predictor, so it does not make the claim.
